newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-KUERTEN DEDICATES SENSATIONAL WIN TO LATE FATHER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KUERTEN DEDICATES SENSATIONAL WIN TO LATE FATHER.

text.p: After charming centre court with a brilliant win over Spaniard Sergi Bruguera in Sunday's French Open final, Brazilian Gustavo Kuerten dedicated his victory to his late father, who died of a heart attack when he was eight.
"He was such an important person for me," said the 20-year-old Kuerten after beating all the odds to become the first Brazilian to win a Grand Slam tournament.
"I was eight when I lost him and at that time I didn't expect to become a tennis player. He was the person I loved the most and this trophy goes to him. I hope he's happy right now."

Kuerten, who beat former champions Austrian Thomas Muster and Russian Yevgeny Kafelnikov of Russia on his way to the final, delighted the Parisian crowd by outclassing two-times winner Bruguera with a spectacular display of attacking tennis.
Before coming to Paris, he had only won a single tournament on the satellite circuit in front of his home fans in Curitiba, Brazil.
Ranked a modest 66 in the world, he was regarded merely as an exotic attraction -- with his long, curly hair and flashy yellow and blue outfit -- when the French Open began.

Steady from the baseline, he stroked stunning winners with his backhand as well as his forehand and mixed his fast game with some clever drop shots and smart volleys. The Brazilian showed he knew every trick in the book.
He also offered a fresh, relaxed attitude, joking with the ball boys and celebrated a winning shot with a little dance.
But the Brazilian, who loves football and likes to go surfing off his southern town of Florianopolis, also provided a cheeky touch.
He did not seem to take it all too seriously.

After wiping his feet free of clay dust before going up to receive the trophy and the winner's cheque of $695,500, he went outside the stadium to listen to a Brazilian band playing samba in his honour and stayed there several minutes to sign autographs.
"I'm not going to change just because I won here," he said. "I'll still be the same guy."
When asked what he planned to do with his prizemoney, Kuerten replied: "I've got all I need right now. I have a good house and my mum's car which I use a little bit."
